page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a constrained-vCPU architecture powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside a total of 48 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 322 GB of local SSD storage and zero GPUs, with instructions supporting AES, SHA-NI, AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the asymmetric design of this constrained-core instance. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1648.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 28.04 GB/sec, and a PassMark encryption test score of 3657.74, achieve average performance within the middle 50% tier. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the 4-vCPU ceiling, placing multi-core stress-ng (3869.36) and Geekbench multi-core (3539.0) in the lower 25%. Decompression and 7B parameter LLM inference are also restricted, reaching poor tiers at 19.79 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 and 4.57 tokens per second for 7B text generation.

Memory throughput registers 30.58 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 25.35 GB/sec for large uncached writes, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2477.65. Application throughput metrics demonstrate 3.95 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.71 GB/sec in static web serving. The inclusion of 322 GB local SSD storage provides direct temporary scratch space, although zero public IPv4 addresses are bundled by default.

The primary tradeoff of the E8-4ds_v5 lies in its specialized resource ratio. By restricting compute to 4 vCPUs while retaining the 64.0 GB memory footprint of an 8-vCPU class host, it provides high cost efficiency for software licensed per core that mandates substantial memory capacity. This profile fits memory-bound databases, in-memory caches such as Redis, enterprise analytics, and ETL workloads that require high RAM density without extensive parallel compute threads.
